_readme: Single source of truth for the five main experience stops. Each renders to work/<slug>.html — the ONLY place that company's full story lives. Cards elsewhere link here.

items.one: Perception data infrastructure: a system that grades ~409 data miners against the human labels they exist to produce — grounded SQL, deterministic verification, zero extra labeling cost.
deep: Automated quality validation for ~409 active miners on a fleet that mines 90M+ events a week from drive logs.

The LLM drafts one scoped SQL true-positive predicate per miner, grounded in the annotation ontology and the label vocabulary actually observed in the warehouse. The generate → execute → verify → retry loop keeps it honest; scoring itself is plain SQL and never calls the model.
321 of 321 ground-truth-capable miners validated at a ~1.3 s median; write-on-change history cut redundant writes ~93%; stored SQL reproduces every number.
Failure discovery went from periodic reviews to minutes: alerts fire on the miner run-state transition to FAILED, with per-owner DMs and a deep link to the run.

Weekly Postgres aggregation into immutable versioned JSON snapshots plus an S3 manifest, read by a zero-backend Vite/TypeScript/Chart.js dashboard and a read-only Slack Q&A that answers only from published snapshots — no tools, fenced untrusted context, Vault-managed credentials.

items.role: M.S. Applied Data Science + Graduate Research Assistant
items.one: Human-centered, attention-aware AI with real deployments: visual-attention measurement, an AI wheelchair obstacle-alert interface, and SO-101 robot learning. RSCA winner; two 2026 posters, one Elsevier article.
deep: Visual attention: a reproducible pipeline over Pupil Labs gaze, fixation, blink and pupil streams across global, selective and sustained tasks; fixation count emerged as the strongest task discriminator. RSCA research-competition winner and SJSU delegate to the 40th CSU Student Research Competition.

Assistive mobility: an AI power-wheelchair obstacle-alert system where the contribution is the human-machine interface — depth-triggered multimodal warnings (twelve tactors plus speech or tone) measured by how fast a real person responds, across 24 participants and 24 trials each.

Robot learning: SO-101 leader/follower arms with Feetech servos — 50 teleoperated demonstrations, ACT trained from scratch and SmolVLA fine-tuning, physical pick-and-place rollouts with video-measured placement error, and the EEPROM Lock=1 fix that unblocked calibration.
Presented at the SJSU AI Center for Civic and Social Good grand opening alongside a faculty advisor.

items.one: Salesforce-driven product analytics for a cloud-security company: a metadata-driven LLM compiler that turns dynamic formula fields into validated, versioned warehouse SQL, plus incremental geospatial ingestion that cut reporting latency ~80%.
deep: The core problem: Salesforce formula fields recompute in real time but don't bump LastModifiedTimestamp, so incremental ingestion kept falling back to full refreshes — slower reports, more compute cost, less trust in the dashboards.

The fix was a compiler, not a prompt: pulled formula definitions via the ObjectDetails API, extracted complete formula logic, ran a depth-first traversal over nested field dependencies, and emitted structured JSON context (dependency graph + formula text) into an LLM that produced optimized SQL, inserted into version-controlled dbt models.

Because LLM-assisted generation adds risk, I engineered the verification: automated sampling that compared transformed warehouse output against the live CRM source, flagged discrepancies programmatically, and drove reconciliation dashboards — 100% validation confidence before deployment.

Redesigned ingestion around incremental upserts and change detection, with partitioning and clustering tuned for Snowflake on location-based attributes; heavy transforms stayed in the warehouse, off the request path.

Integrated LinkedIn Campaign, Asana and Jira APIs into the analytics pipeline with normalized schemas and dashboards; Git-based CI with automated schema checks and SQL tests via GitHub Actions and Docker.

numbers.v: faster queries at lower warehouse cost

items.one: Enterprise analytics consulting at petabyte scale: controlled migration of ~800 TB from HDFS to S3 behind a Delta Lake validation gate, with CloudWatch/SNS/Lambda SLA enforcement that cut client escalations ~45%.
deep: The migration: ~800 TB of enterprise data moved from HDFS to AWS S3, with AWS Data Sync handling the transfer and bash scripts tracking and validating every copied batch.

Controlled, not fire-and-forget: a Delta Lake–style validation framework with Python and pytest-style dataset checks diffed source and destination for row mismatches, null anomalies and type drift — 99.6% validation accuracy before go-live, which is what kept it from becoming a client escalation.
SLAs: CloudWatch metrics, SNS alerting and reactive Lambda triggers orchestrated in Airflow; root-cause traces cut time-to-detection of pipeline failures, reducing client escalations by ~45%.

Performance: layered CTE rewrites, partitioning and execution optimization took a major reporting pipeline from ~18 minutes to 6; containerized operators and modular DAGs moved legacy Airflow pipelines to managed (MWAA-style) environments.

items.one: Production Spring Boot backend for a healthcare client: microservice tuning, PostgreSQL schema and index work behind Liquibase, and Docker/GitLab CI — the foundation for everything after.
deep: Backend microservices refactored for concurrency: thread handling, connection pooling and caching cut request failures by ~33% and steadied peak responses.
Database work: inefficient joins reduced, indexing strategy redesigned, Liquibase migrations version-controlled — a 2.5× query performance improvement and more predictable load.
Release hygiene: Dockerized services and GitLab CI pipelines cut the release cycle by ~17% and removed the 'works on my machine' class of failures.
